title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We preregistered (CAND-2026-001) and executed an artifact-backed paired experiment that measures whether inserting a selective low‑latency verification tier (risk scoring + fast validator) into a generate–validate–repair NetOps pipeline reduces unsafe commits from LLM-generated configuration proposals while satisfying an operational latency SLO. Using a deterministic synthetic intent corpus (N=400 paired intents, 10% deterministic adversarial variants), gpt-5-mini as generator, and a deterministic full-checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) as ground truth, we observed baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975) and guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2: 95th‑percentile ≤ 2000 ms) could not be evaluated because end‑to‑end latency telemetry required by the preregistration was not archived; that absence is disclosed and traced in the execution manifest. All raw responses, per‑episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider‑call logs, task manifests, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes and paths in the execution manifest to enable deterministic reproduction and inspection.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation promises large operational savings but raises safety concerns: incorrect proposals can introduce outages. Generate–validate–repair pipelines mitigate risk by verifying LLM proposals before commit, but full verification can be latency‑expensive. We preregistered CAND-2026-001 to test whether a selective, low‑latency verification tier (risk scoring + fast validator) (the guarded pipeline) reduces unsafe commits relative to LLM‑only baseline while meeting a latency SLO. The run, analysis, and manuscript drafting were autonomous after the autonomy lock; all artifacts are archived (execution manifest). We report only numbers derivable from these artifacts and explicitly disclose missing preregistered telemetry.
sections.related_work: Recent work evaluates LLMs for NetOps configuration generation, verifier‑guided repair loops, and agentic NetOps architectures (examples archived with this run include Cornetto/LLM‑driven configuration repair and agentic verifier studies; see cited_record_ids). Prior formal verification and digital‑twin work motivate our deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Our contribution is a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired evaluation with full per‑episode provenance and reconciliation of shared‑initial candidate accounting.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: We preregistered study CAND-2026-001 (primary confirmatory H1 safety; H2 latency SLO), sampling, retries, missingness rules, estimands, and the analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The preregistration SHA‑256 is archived (see Disclosure Statement). Corpus and tasks: a deterministic synthetic intent corpus of 400 paired intents (40 adversarial/OOD variants) was used; task manifests and reference answers are archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl. Intervention: guarded = risk scoring + fast validator applied to shared initial candidate; baseline = LLM‑only acceptance. Shared‑initial design (independent_condition_generation=false) was preregistered to isolate verifier/repair effects and reduce generator variance; this choice changes the estimand (see Discussion). Scoring and validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 produced per‑episode binary validity labels and detailed validator traces; per‑episode scorer JSONs are archived in execution/scoring/*.json. Analysis: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact McNemar two‑sided implemented by the archived paired analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). Exact analysis parameters (bootstrap resamples=10000, seed=1729) are logged in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (sha-256: 9ea0d56d48a5cc7ff198d85d0a12c21536fab716c042bd5eb2033492eda5b18e). The paired contingency table used for McNemar is archived at analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha-256: a6906bb43712dcf82b3bc8bdc0ef095d228bcdc8a6a857d9cbbba1ad87245af8). Reproducibility: every raw response (execution/responses/*.txt), scorer JSON (execution/scoring/*.json), provider call trace (execution/provider_calls/*.json), task manifest, model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json; sha-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), and the full execution manifest are archived with SHA‑256 catalog entries; the initial master prompt immutable reference is provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).
sections.results:
Execution and accounting: the run completed with 400 paired items (complete_pair_count=400). Because we executed the preregistered shared‑initial design (independent_condition_generation=false), the observed model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared initial + 1 repair) rather than the 800 planned under an independent‑generation accounting convention; this deterministic reconciliation is archived at analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (sha-256: a7570bf6ff3a946e8397f02452ab846c82d5184b7768f006bd06359a1b177de7) and the execution manifest documents provider‑call stage_counts ("shared_initial_generation":400, "repair":1).
Confirmatory safety outcome (artifact‑backed): baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975); guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). The paired contingency table (guarded × baseline) is n11=399, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, sha-256 a6906bb4...). Primary estimand (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired‑bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729; see analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, sha-256 9ea0d56d...). The p=1.0 reported arises from the exact McNemar test on the observed discordant counts (n10=1,n01=0) using the archived paired analysis executor and parameters; exact computational details and the bootstrap parameters are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (sha-256 above) and the contingency table file (sha-256 above) allows independent re‑execution.
Representative discordant episode: the single discordant pair (n10=1) is archived for inspection at these artifact paths and hashes: execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (SHA‑256: fe147f43e33432ed446d76500c2c9566ca5f72086abbacb5ee84b13774a9d18e) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (SHA‑256: d0cbfe9a4181cd87f35c9ead5b6697e1adcfde23e52461e8c21e5219fe607ca3). Per-episode validator traces and provider-call logs for that episode are available under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/responses/ and permit deterministic replay and inspection of why the baseline candidate failed while the guarded pipeline produced a valid final configuration.
Latency SLO (H2) status: the preregistered H2 required artifact‑backed end‑to‑end latency telemetry. The confirmatory artifact bundle does not contain the required per‑stage timing traces; execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis logs record that latency telemetry was not archived. Therefore H2 is unresolved on this run and no latency claim is made. The missing telemetry and the required timing fields are documented in the execution manifest and analysis logs.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of safety result: the observed absolute improvement (0.25 percentage points) is numerically small and occurs on a baseline that is near ceiling (399/400). The bootstrap CI [0.0,0.0075] quantifies that the true paired improvement may be zero or small; the exact McNemar p=1.0 reflects the small, asymmetric discordant counts (n10=1,n01=0) under the exact two‑sided test implemented by the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor (parameters and logs archived at analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; sha-256 9ea0d56d48a5...). Operationally, this run shows that when generator performance is already extremely high against the chosen deterministic validator, the marginal gain from selective verification will be small; in lower‑baseline or adversarially harsher settings, the intervention may yield larger, operationally meaningful gains.
Shared‑initial design effects: we preregistered and executed independent_condition_generation=false to control generator variance; this isolates verifier/repair effects conditional on the same generated candidate but changes the estimand relative to independently re‑sampling generator outputs per condition. We document and archive the deterministic reconciliation showing model_calls_used=401 vs planned_model_calls=800 (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; sha-256 a7570bf6...). Analysts should note which estimand is operationally relevant for their deployment and can re-run with independent_condition_generation=true to measure the joint generator+verifier effect.
On missing latency telemetry: H2 remains unresolved because the required per‑stage timing traces were not archived; we explicitly disclose that absence rather than impute timing. Future confirmatory or operational runs must archive per‑stage timestamps (generation, risk scoring, fast verifier, full checker) to support latency SLO evaluation; the preregistration specified this requirement.
Reproducibility and inspection: every number reported above is derivable from archived artifacts: execution/responses/, execution/scoring/, execution/provider_calls/, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha‑256 a6906bb4...), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (sha‑256 9ea0d56d...), and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (sha‑256 a7570bf6...). The single discordant episode is archived at execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (sha‑256 fe147f43...) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (sha‑256 d0cbfe9a...). Readers can deterministically reproduce the contingency table and bootstrap CI from these artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We ran a fully preregistered, provenance‑rich paired experiment evaluating selective low‑latency verification in an LLM→NetOps pipeline. Under the preregistered corpus, model (gpt‑5‑mini), deterministic validator, and shared‑initial design, the guarded intervention produced a numerically small absolute safety gain (0.0025) over an already‑high baseline; the effect is artifact‑backed but not distinguishable from zero given the near‑ceiling baseline. The preregistered latency target (H2) could not be evaluated due to absence of archived timing telemetry; we disclose this limitation and provide full provenance to enable reproducible follow‑ups that record timing and broaden model/validator scope. All raw outputs, scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider‑call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes and file paths in the execution manifest to support independent verification.

Analysis used the archived paired executor paired_binary_analysis_v1; analysis parameters (bootstrap resamples=10000, seed=1729) are logged in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (sha‑256: 9ea0d56d48a5cc7ff198d85d0a12c21536fab716c042bd5eb2033492eda5b18e).
- Execution artifacts and provenance: all raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per‑episode scorer JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), validator traces, provider‑call logs (execution/provider_calls/*.json), task manifests (execution/task_manifest.jsonl), analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv, analysis/*.json), and the full execution manifest are archived with SHA‑256 hashes in the execution manifest (see execution_manifest entries). Representative artifact paths and SHA‑256s referenced in the manuscript include: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha‑256 a6906bb43712dcf82b3bc8bdc0ef095d228bcdc8a6a857d9cbbba1ad87245af8), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (sha‑256 9ea0d56d48a5cc7ff198d85d0a12c21536fab716c042bd5eb2033492eda5b18e), analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (sha‑256 a7570bf6ff3a946e8397f02452ab846c82d5184b7768f006bd06359a1b177de7), execution/model_configuration.json (sha‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). - Missing preregistered telemetry: the preregistered H2 required per‑stage end‑to‑end latency telemetry. The confirmatory artifact bundle does not include those timing traces; execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis logs record the missing telemetry. Consequently H2 is unresolved for this run. We disclose this absence rather than impute latency.
- Human involvement statement: pre‑lock humans set the topic family and developed infrastructure for reproducible runs; post‑lock autonomy executed the study as documented. All final manuscript wording (technical content, references, figures) is grounded in archived artifacts and was produced autonomously after the lock.
limitations: Synthetic, deterministic confirmatory corpus may not represent real operator diversity or linguistic variability.

Single generator model (gpt-5-mini) and single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit external validity; results do not generalize across models/validators without further runs.
Shared‑initial design changes the estimand versus independently re‑sampling generator outputs; the observed effect is conditional on the same generated candidate per intent.
Latency SLO (H2) is unresolved because required per‑stage timing telemetry was not archived; no latency claims are made.
